transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to call this huddle together so we can review the health and family-access details for the new food pantry before it opens next month. We've got a solid draft operating plan on the table — it covers refrigerated and shelf-stable food, weekly temperature checks, and our district's standard labeling procedure. On the access side, student pickup is scheduled during lunch on Wednesdays, and intake materials will be available in English and Spanish. I'd like to walk through each of these areas and make sure we haven't missed anything before we finalize the plan. Who'd like to start — should we begin with the health and safety details or the family-access side?

transcript.text: I'd like to start with the health and safety details, because I have some important county health guidance that hasn't made it into the draft plan yet. I reviewed the county health guidance for the pantry this week, and there are two key requirements we're missing. First, refrigerated food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or colder, and the temperature needs to be logged every 2 hours while the pantry is open — our current draft only calls for a weekly temperature check, which won't meet that standard. Second, sealed packages must display allergen labels. I have the printed guidance in my health-office binder and can share it with everyone so we can update the draft accordingly.

transcript.text: I appreciate the health and safety updates, and I have some important family-access information to share as well. I completed family outreach this week, and I found that Thursday from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. is the only pickup window that works for the participating households. Also, intake materials need to be available in English, Spanish, and Somali — not just English and Spanish as the draft currently states. I haven't yet updated the operations sheet with these outreach results, so I wanted to make sure everyone here has this information before we finalize the plan.
